chunks: ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and Marthad ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī would take turns riding one camel among themselves while they were setting out toward Badr.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.بَدْرٍ: Badr, the destination of the expedition and site of the famous battle
key_terms.بَعِيرًا: A camel used for riding and travel
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام travel on the way to Badr?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and Marthad ibn Abī Marthad al-Ghanawī shared a single camel on the way to Badr. It reflects simplicity, solidarity, and the lived sunnah of humility during an important historical expedition.
